title: Question 10
stem: Explain the photoelectric effect and calculate threshold wavelengths.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the photoelectric effect.

markscheme_points.text: electromagnetic radiation / photons incident on a metal surface
causes emission of electrons from the surface

hints: Hint 1: Recall the formal Cambridge definition regarding photoelectric effect. State clearly the physical conditions and quantities involved.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: electromagnetic radiation / photons incident on a metal surface; causes emission of electrons from the surface

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the energy of a photon of wavelength $436\text{ nm}$.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in photoelectric effect connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Photoelectric effect. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
$E = hc / \lambda = (6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 3.00 \times 10^8) / (436 \times 10^{-9})$; $E = 4.56 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: The work function of caesium is $1.4\text{ eV}$. Calculate its threshold wavelength.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in photoelectric effect connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Photoelectric effect. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
$\Phi = hc / \lambda_0 \implies \lambda_0 = (6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 3.00 \times 10^8) / (1.4 \times 1.60 \times 10^{-19})$; $\lambda_0 = 890\text{ nm}$
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: State and explain whether photoelectric emission occurs for caesium and for tungsten when illuminated with light of wavelength $436\text{ nm}$.

markscheme_points.text: caesium: photon wavelength ($436\text{ nm}$) is less than threshold wavelength ($890\text{ nm}$), so emission occurs
tungsten: photon wavelength ($436\text{ nm}$) is greater than threshold wavelength ($280\text{ nm}$), so no emission occurs
